 Advertisement Bob Uecker’s legacy looms large as Brewers reach World Series
 Advertisement Updated: 5:56 PM CDT Oct 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ James Ganley Bob Uecker’s legacy looms large as Brewers reach World Series
 Updated: 5:56 PM CDT Oct 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ James Ganley MILWAUKEE — WORLD SERIES GUIDE | SCHEDULE | MERCH | WATCH PARTIES | TICKETS | FORECAST | POP CULTURE IN 1982 | VIRAL SONG | PAINTING THE FIELD | AVOIDING SCAMS 
 As the Brewers celebrated their first World Series berth since 1982 , they also remembered Bob Uecker, the longtime voice of the team who died in 2025.
 Advertisement Milwaukee beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 Thursday night to complete an NLCS sweep, prompting tributes to Uecker from team leaders who knew how much the moment would have meant to him. 
 “We’re standing on shoulders of Bud Selig and Bob Uecker,” Brewers principal owner Mark Attanasio said as he accepted the National League Championship trophy on Thursday night at Dodgers Stadium.
 Where to buy Brewers World Series and NLCS champs merchandise Uecker died Jan. 16, 2025 , at age 90 after battling lung cancer. He spent 54 seasons broadcasting Brewers baseball, becoming a familiar companion to generations of fans. 
 His connection to the Brewers and Milwaukee extended well beyond the radio booth. Those who knew him knew how much a championship would have meant to him.
 “He’d be so happy for the guys,” manager Pat Murphy said after the emotional win.
 “Those who knew him well are all thinking about Ueck today because, ya know, he helped us. He knocked that ball down in that first game to let us know he was there and he was watching. So his presence was known. I’m really happy because I know he’s up there smiling.”
 Murphy was referring to a towering Padres fly ball that struck the roof at American Family Field and dropped into Jackson Chourio’s glove during the NLDS opener.
 Brewers edge Padres 3-2 in NLDS opener that features bizarre play in 9th inning Former Brewers pitcher and Hall of Famer CC Sabathia also remembered Uecker on social media, saying he wished Uecker were here to see it.

 The Brewers shared their own tribute to their longtime broadcaster during the celebration.
 This content is imported from x. You may be able to find the same content in another format, or you may be able to find more information, at their web site. Dedicating this Pennant to Mr. Baseball 💙 pic.twitter.com/zDdHlmIVTf 
— Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 16, 2026 
 Uecker’s former broadcast partner Jeff Levering called Thursday’s final out, and his words carried an echo of Uecker as Milwaukee celebrated its return to the World Series.
 "The Brewers win the pennant! Oh my God, the Brewers win the pennant!" Levering shouted as Jackson Chourio caught the final out in left field.
 The call echoed Uecker's celebration as fictional Cleveland announcer Harry Doyle in "Major League."
 The Harry Doyle role introduced Uecker to generations of movie fans, but his national fame extended well beyond the baseball comedies. He played George Owens on the sitcom "Mr. Belvedere," became a familiar face in Miller Lite commercials and made frequent appearances alongside Johnny Carson on "The Tonight Show." Carson gave him the nickname "Mr. Baseball."
 SWEEP: Brewers headed to the World Series for first time since 1982 Now the Brewers have a chance to bring home the championship "Mr. Baseball" wanted for Milwaukee.
 October baseball is back in Milwaukee, and WISN 12 News is covering every inning, in the stands and across the community. We're following the Brewers’ postseason run to the World Series, bringing you the biggest moments, the players driving the story and the traditions that unite fans.
